main_text.p: vestra: ex Jef.5.12. Amplificetur ex fine creatio-nis hominis.
II. Quia exstincto rationis usu inflammat cupiditates, iram; odium: libidinem, &c. quibus ebriosi bestiarum more ad scelera abripiuntur & deformantur: Eph.5.18.
Illustretur exemplis Sodomitarum, Lothi, Alexandri Magni, Nohę: M. Antonii sępe[?] vomentis pro tribunali;
Addantur dicta Senecæ: Ebrietas voluntaria insania: Et: Habitus ebrietatis extensus in plures dies est furor. Et ejusdem Epiphonema. Multa faciunt ebrii, quorum postea sobrios pudet.
Probetur II. pernicies itidem ab effectis.
II. Perdit rem domesticam: cum injuria conjugum & liberorum. Prov.21.17.
III. Generat morbos: febrem: podagram, hydropem. Prov.23.
IV. Accelerat mortem: sæpe violentam ac turpem,
V. Pervertit judicia Prov.31.5. Lex Solonis capitis pœnam irrogavit principi ebrio.
VI. Evertit regna & respub. securitate. Joel, 1.5.Ief.5.Amos 5.7.
main_text.head: Exercitatio IX.

head.i: An fœdera cum impiis sint licita.

main_text.p: EXordium ex præcepto Pauli: Nolite trahere

page.notes: The Greek word after "Conclusio: sit" is a small, hard-to-read print; the reading ὑποδιωξις is a best guess. The "3" after "iugum" at the foot is a stray mark, not transcribed. The "Ief" references and the "sępe" / "Nohę" forms are read from a small, slightly blurred print and may be misread. The first letter "E" of "Exordium" is a large initial. The printed "I I." and "I." numerals are rendered as II. The page ends mid-sentence on "trahere".
